name: Heme synthesis
summary: Bone marrow (erythroid precursors) and liver. Starts and ends in mitochondria; the middle steps are cytosolic. ALA synthase is rate-limiting and repressed by heme. Lead inhibits ALA dehydratase and ferrochelatase. Each enzyme deficiency past ALA dehydratase is a porphyria.

glycine.name: Glycine
glycine.notes: Condenses with succinyl-CoA (from the TCA cycle).

ala.name: δ-Aminolevulinic acid
ala.notes: Exits the mitochondrion. Elevated in lead poisoning and acute intermittent porphyria.

pbg.name: Porphobilinogen
pbg.notes: Four PBG units build the tetrapyrrole. ↑ urinary PBG = acute intermittent porphyria.

hmb.name: Hydroxymethylbilane
hmb.notes: Linear tetrapyrrole; spontaneously cyclizes to uroporphyrinogen I without the next enzyme.

uro.name: Uroporphyrinogen III
uro.notes: ↑ in porphyria cutanea tarda (urine looks tea-colored).

proto.name: Protoporphyrin IX
proto.notes: ↑ (as zinc protoporphyrin) in lead poisoning and iron deficiency.

heme.name: Heme
heme.notes: Represses ALA synthase (and hemin is given in acute porphyria attacks for that reason).

alas.name: ALA synthase
alas.notes: Rate-limiting; needs B6 (pyridoxal phosphate). Repressed by heme; induced by drugs that use cytochrome P450 (barbiturates, etc.). ALAS2 (erythroid) defects or B6 deficiency (isoniazid) → sideroblastic anemia.

alad.name: ALA dehydratase
alad.notes: Joins two ALA. Inhibited by lead (↑ ALA → neuro symptoms, basophilic stippling with ferrochelatase block).

pbgd.name: Porphobilinogen deaminase
pbgd.notes: Deficiency → acute intermittent porphyria (AD): painful abdomen, port-wine urine, polyneuropathy, psychological symptoms, precipitated by drugs/alcohol/starvation. No photosensitivity. Treat with glucose and hemin.

uros.name: Uroporphyrinogen III synthase
uros.notes: Deficiency → congenital erythropoietic porphyria (Günther): severe photosensitivity, red urine and teeth.

urod.name: Uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase
urod.notes: Deficiency → porphyria cutanea tarda, the most common porphyria: blistering photosensitivity, hyperpigmentation, hypertrichosis, tea-colored urine; triggered by alcohol, hepatitis C, iron overload, estrogens.

fech.name: Ferrochelatase
fech.notes: Inserts Fe²⁺. Inhibited by lead (→ ↑ zinc protoporphyrin). Deficiency → erythropoietic protoporphyria (painful, non-blistering photosensitivity).
